an1.378:1.1: The first four of these are austere practices. Listed as thirteen in later texts ([mil6.4.2](), [pli-tv-pvr17:128.1]()), they are scattered through the Suttas and Vinaya. They are regarded as virtuous practices to undertake voluntarily, often for a limited period of time.
an1.379:1.1: Relying on alms was normal, but monastics might also accept an invitation to eat in a donor’s home, or else food brought to the monastery by donors. One following this rule would reject such meal offerings.
an1.380:1.1: Robe cloth could be recovered, especially after being used for draping corpses in the cemetery. The monastic would clean it, cut off any damaged parts, sew a robe of patches, and dye it the proper color.
an1.381:1.1: While three robes are mandated under Vinaya (under robe, upper robe, and outer cloak), monastics often have extra cloth for bathing, shoulder-cloths, and so on. An adherent of this practice would use only the three.
